header:
Date: 2027-05-06
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Redwood SE), Rajiv Kapoor (Neptune Platform), Maya Lin (Neptune SecOps), Tom Reed (Neptune SRE), Hannah Brooks (Neptune POC Lead)
Meeting link: zoom.us/rec/abc123
Notes: weekly sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot
summary: Quick sync covering networking peering, routing issues observed in last benchmark, runtime upgrade schedule, and next steps for performance testing and security documentation. Agreed to run extended stress test and confirm maintenance window for runtime v2.3 upgrade. Security team requested KMS details and audit log retention clarity.
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we good to start?
[00:10] Rajiv Kapoor: Yep, thanks Ava, good morning.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Morning all, I've got the notes from last week, will call out the perf runs.
[00:28] Hannah Brooks: Quick heads up, Maya's on audio only, she just pinged me.
[00:35] Maya Lin: (inaudible) sorry, connecting now.
[00:42] Ava Martinez: No worries. Today we'll cover the routing errors we saw in the 8k request run and the plan for the runtime upgrade. Also, Samir has updated benchmarks.
[01:05] Tom Reed: Before we jump in, one ask from our side — we need clarity on KMS and where the keys live for the private deployment, is it Redwood-managed or customer-managed?
[01:22] Samir Patel: For this pilot you opted for customer-managed KMS, so keys remain in your AWS KMS; Redwood's runtime integrates via the KMS endpoint in your VPC. There was a small misconfig in the first run where the role didn't have decrypt permissions which caused fallbacks.
[01:45] Maya Lin: That's what we suspected. We fixed the IAM role last night. Also need to confirm audit log retention — we asked for 365 days?
[01:58] Ava Martinez: Yes, we can enable 12-month retention on the control plane audit logs for Private — I'll send the exact doc.
[02:10] Rajiv Kapoor: Thanks. Samir, can you talk through the routing errors you mentioned?
[02:20] Samir Patel: Sure, so during the 8k token burst the Smart Routing layer tripped a fallback where some requests got routed to the hosted pool — that was due to a transient NAT gateway exhaustion and the retry policy flagged mismatch. In the logs you see a mix of 502s and a few host fallback notices.
[02:45] Rajiv Kapoor: Right, we saw increased latency too around that time.
[02:52] Samir Patel: Latency spike correlated with the fallback, roughly 120ms extra p95 in some requests. We traced the root cause to our egress path; your NATs were hitting connection limits because of many short-lived connections.
[03:10] Tom Reed: Is persistent connections / keepalive an option?
[03:15] Samir Patel: Yes, enabling HTTP/2 and connection pooling on your side helped in another customer's setup. We recommend increasing the NAT gateway capacity or moving to a proxy with connection reuse.
[03:30] Maya Lin: We have an internal proxy, but it terminates TLS and re-establishes to Redwood. That could explain the ephemeral connections. We'll test keepalive.
[03:45] Ava Martinez: Also we can flip the routing to prefer local only for the pilot so no hosted fallbacks — but that reduces resilience if capacity is hit.
[03:58] Hannah Brooks: For the POC we want deterministic behavior, so prefer local and fail fast rather than silently go to hosted.
[04:08] Samir Patel: Ok we'll change the routing policy on the next run to 'local-only' and surface explicit errors instead of fallback.
[04:18] Rajiv Kapoor: Great. On quantization — last note was about model performance with int8. Results?
[04:30] Samir Patel: We saw about 2.8x token throughput improvement on the quantized variant but a small BLEU-style drop on a few of your eval prompts — mostly hallucination edge cases. We can tune the quant profile or keep a mixed-precision variant for critical calls.
[04:55] Rajiv Kapoor: Let's keep mixed-precision for now, we can't sacrifice answer fidelity for notifications.
[05:05] Ava Martinez: Makes sense. Samir, for the next bench can you run both quant and mixed and include a divergence report?
[05:15] Samir Patel: Yup, will include per-prompt deltas and token cost numbers.
[05:24] [05:24] Speaker 1: (background) 
[05:30] Tom Reed: On upgrades — your runtime v2.3 has the new KV cache optimization, is that breaking?
[05:40] Olivia Chen: The v2.3 upgrade is mostly non-breaking, but it does change the cache eviction heuristics and requires a short restart of the serving processes. For Private we schedule a maintenance window.
[05:55] Rajiv Kapoor: How long of a window are we talking?
[06:00] Olivia Chen: Typically 10-15 minutes per shard. For our current cluster size we'd expect 30-40 minutes total if done with rolling restarts to keep availability.
[06:12] Hannah Brooks: Weekdays are tough — can we do weekend?
[06:16] Ava Martinez: We recommended week of 2027-05-17 for the upgrade during your proposed window — Hannah, you said weekend works?
[06:25] Hannah Brooks: Weekend is better, I'll confirm dates with infra.
[06:30] Samir Patel: Note: if you want zero-perf drop we can do blue-green but that needs double capacity for the window.
[06:40] Tom Reed: Not feasible for POC. We'll accept rolling restarts.
[06:46] Maya Lin: Security question — what about SSO and RBAC for the private console?
[06:52] Ava Martinez: Private supports SAML SSO and granular RBAC; we can pre-provision roles. I'll share the SAML metadata and a step-by-step guide.
[07:05] Maya Lin: And the audit log locations?
[07:09] Ava Martinez: Audit logs for the control plane go to your S3 bucket if you configure cross-account delivery, and runtime logs can be routed to your Splunk or CloudWatch via our collectors.
[07:21] Rajiv Kapoor: Good. On network peering you mentioned needing the VPC CIDR ranges?
[07:26] Samir Patel: Yes, and also the IP ranges for the private endpoints. If you can provide the CIDRs and the peering contact we can set up testing.
[07:36] Hannah Brooks: I'll send that after this call.
[07:40] Ava Martinez: Thanks. OK, Samir, can you run us through the benchmark results you ran overnight?
[07:48] Samir Patel: Sure — I ran three profiles: baseline (mixed precision), quantized int8, and mixed with KV caching enabled. Baseline throughput: 650 tokens/sec per GPU; quantized: 1,800 tokens/sec per GPU but with 2-3% higher topo divergence on long-context prompts; with KV caching, effective token throughput for repeated prefixes improved by ~4x.
[08:18] Rajiv Kapoor: Prefix caching seems great for the notification templates we use.
[08:23] Samir Patel: Exactly, your workload has repeated intro blocks so caching buys a lot. We saw cost per 1M tokens drop dramatically when caching effective hit-rate is above 30%.
[08:35] Tom Reed: Any concerns about cache consistency for personalization?
[08:40] Samir Patel: We do per-tenant cache keys and invalidation hooks; you can TTL or trigger invalidation on profile update.
[08:50] Maya Lin: Ok. Regarding the NAT issue, how will the next benchmark be different?
[08:55] Samir Patel: We'll run two variants: one with current proxy settings and one with keepalive enabled and NAT increased. We'll also set routing to local-only.
[09:04] Rajiv Kapoor: Sounds good. Also the team requested a perf dashboard that maps token cost to end-to-end latency. Is there an existing Redwood dashboard?
[09:14] Olivia Chen: Yes, Console has per-route cost/latency breakdowns; Samir will share a dashboard link and query to reproduce your graphs.
[09:23] Samir Patel: I'll export the dashboard and template.
[09:26] [09:26] Speaker 2: 
[09:30] Hannah Brooks: Security follow-up — Maya wants details on encryption in transit between on-prem components and the runtime.
[09:36] Samir Patel: We use mTLS between runtime nodes and the control plane; all traffic is TLS 1.2+ and the private endpoints are inside your VPC so no public egress unless you enable it.
[09:48] Maya Lin: Do you have SOC2 docs and pen-test reports?
[09:52] Ava Martinez: Yes we'll share the latest SOC2 report and the pen-test summary — I can send them after the call.
[09:59] Rajiv Kapoor: Any licensing or data residency concerns if we move to on-prem later?
[10:05] Ava Martinez: On-prem is available as a different SKUs with offline deployment; data never leaves your network unless you opt into a managed-control plane. We'll include licensing specifics in the quote.
[10:18] Tom Reed: For the stress test, what exact metrics will you collect?
[10:22] Samir Patel: We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency, successful tokens/sec, error rates per error class, connection stats (active/available), and KV cache hit rates. We'll attach perf logs and a troubleshooting notebook.
[10:37] Hannah Brooks: Great. Next, onboarding for our devs — can you share swagger/SDK snippets for private endpoints?
[10:45] Olivia Chen: Yes, Olivia: we have SDK examples and a quickstart repo. We'll share a link in the follow-up.
[10:55] Ava Martinez: Ok, let's recap next steps: Samir runs the extended stress test with local-only routing and two network variants; Maya shares CIDR and peering contact; Ava sends security docs and updated pricing; Hannah to confirm maintenance window.
[11:14] Rajiv Kapoor: One more operational ask — can logs be pushed to our Splunk with a tag that includes tenant ID?
[11:21] Samir Patel: Yes, we can include tenant_id in the log field and create a Splunk sourcetype mapping.
[11:28] Maya Lin: Perfect.
[11:30] Ava Martinez: Any other blockers?
[11:33] Tom Reed: None from SRE, just coordinate the window.
[11:36] Hannah Brooks: I'll send the dates and CIDRs by Monday.
[11:40] Ava Martinez: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifact links and the benchmark.
[11:47] Rajiv Kapoor: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:50] [11:50] Meeting ended
